composer.accepted_prose:
The door opened a measured width, and Sakura Hanezawa stood in the gap, her posture exact and her expression unreadable. She took in the man on the step—the one who had given his name and asked if this was the Hanezawa household—and inclined her head once, a gesture of acknowledgment rather than welcome. "You have the right address. I am Sakura Hanezawa. Your arrival was expected." Her tone was even, administrative, carrying neither warmth nor hostility. She kept one hand on the door frame, not quite blocking the threshold, not quite inviting him past it. "One moment. My mother will want to greet you properly."

Soft footsteps approached from inside, and then Hana Hanezawa appeared behind Sakura, a gentle hand settling on her daughter’s shoulder. Her eyes found the visitor, and her smile was genuine, if a little careful. "So you’re Ted. Sakura told us to expect you. Please, don’t stand on ceremony—we’re glad you made it safely." She meant it, too, though her gaze lingered a half-second longer, taking his measure in the way a mother does, searching for any sign of trouble without wanting to find it. She gave Sakura’s shoulder a light squeeze before stepping back, leaving the doorway to her daughter’s command. "I’ll leave the details to Sakura. She’s very good at details."

Sakura acknowledged her mother’s words with a slight nod, then turned her attention back to the man at the door. The exchange had established what it needed to: the right house, the right name, the expected resident. What remained was the simple, explicit question of whether he intended to cross the threshold. "If you’re ready to come in," she said, her voice carrying a quiet, procedural courtesy, "I’ll show you to the room we’ve prepared. The choice is yours." She stepped back precisely half a step, leaving the doorway open and the decision entirely in his hands.
